claims.text: 2.25Cr–1Mo is a low-alloy steel used in nuclear applications.
Conventionally processed 2.25Cr–1Mo steel has a baseline passive film and characteristic grain-boundary precipitate distribution.
Controlled additions of Mo and W segregate during processing and thermal exposure.
Mo and W additions promote discrete, stable intermetallic precipitates in the steel.
Mo and W additions enrich or otherwise alter the passive oxide film at grain boundaries.
The precipitates and modified oxide produce a denser, microstructurally ordered interfacial barrier.
The modified interfacial barrier reduces ionic diffusivity along grain boundaries.
Reduced grain-boundary ionic transport limits pathways for corrosive attack.
The Mo/W-induced microstructural and oxide changes enhance corrosion resistance under nuclear reactor water chemistry.
Mo/W-modified specimens will exhibit slower corrosion kinetics than the baseline steel.
Mo/W-modified specimens will exhibit less intergranular attack than the baseline steel.
Mo/W-modified specimens will form a more uniform and less defective passive film than the baseline steel.
A lower corrosion-current density is evidence of improved corrosion resistance.
Autoclave exposure at approximately 300°C and high pressure can represent relevant nuclear reactor coolant conditions.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold under controlled high-temperature nuclear reactor water chemistry.
The mechanism may not apply under strongly acidic or highly oxidizing chemical-processing conditions.
Industrial processing may introduce variability in the uniformity of the proposed microalloying effects.
Failure to obtain statistically significant corrosion improvement, or observation of passive-film degradation, would falsify the proposed hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The nominal baseline is 2.25Cr–1Mo steel, which already contains Mo, but the intervention and experimental design describe Mo together with W as absent from the baseline and present only in the modified specimens. The intended additional Mo concentration and whether W alone or both elements distinguish the groups are not defined.
